machine_approved.method: Shaped with uharfbuzz in both shipped fonts (kerning disabled — the rebuild has no kern feature until its own milestone, so the old font's kerning is comparison noise) under every config in the unit's set; outlines decomposed with fontTools DecomposingRecordingPen, translated by the cumulative x_advance plus each glyph's x_offset/y_offset, sorted, and compared — the placed ink is identical under every config, so only glyph names differ.

ink_identical.method: Shaped with uharfbuzz in both shipped fonts (kerning disabled — the rebuild has no kern feature until its own milestone, so the old font's kerning is comparison noise) under every config in the unit's set; outlines decomposed with fontTools DecomposingRecordingPen, translated by the cumulative x_advance plus each glyph's x_offset/y_offset, sorted, and compared — the placed ink is identical under every config, so only glyph names differ.

junior_equivalent.method: Divergent only under ss10 (suppress all joins), where the ratified spec is fully isolated letters; shaped with uharfbuzz in the rebuild under ss10 and in the shipped Junior font (the canonical isolated rendering) with no features, kern-neutral on both sides; outlines decomposed, placed, and compared after removing Junior's uniform one-pixel-per-letter tracking (verified against the shipped Senior at construction) — the rebuild draws every letter exactly as Junior draws it in isolation.

classes.why: The ratified boundary-equals-word-boundary rule (ZWNJ 2026-07-03, extended to space the same day, generalizing design section 3.4): a window containing a run-splitting boundary — space or ZWNJ — never needs its own verdict. Post-boundary is definitionally word-initial and pre-boundary definitionally word-final, so the new font renders every segment of a boundary window identically to that segment standing alone — a guarantee that lives in the font's vetting code, not in this transitional ledger: run_boundary_equivalence enforces it per build over the exhaustive enumeration for every splits_runs token (with the namer-dot carve-out removed — the dot no longer lowers through a ZWNJ, the last cross-boundary behavior), and the rune schema admits neither `is: zwnj` nor `is: space`, so no record can ever distinguish a run-splitting boundary from a text edge. A boundary row can therefore only diverge from the baseline in two ways, neither adjudicable here: a segment-internal divergence, which resurfaces on the segment's own enumerated row (every segment of a length-≤5 window is itself a length-≤5 window), or the old font's boundary-context-only inconsistency (the post-ZWNJ shadow universe — post-space ·Utter·May joins at y0 while post-ZWNJ joined at y5 — and its space-side counterpart), which is exactly what the rule retires — unrecoverable by design, since honoring it would resurrect a boundary-conditioned form. ZWNJ evidence: subsumes the ZWNJ share of the former zwnj-word-initial-unification (round-1: 1,421 ink-identical rows), zwnj-follower-exit-restored (reviewed-approved), and zwnj-word-initial-seam-moved classes, and the round-2 re-adjudication of the same-question-twice pairs (u-15220 approve vs u-15230 reject on identical new ink) that motivated the rule. Space evidence: of the 744 space units verdicted on the pre-blanket surface (679 approve / 32 reject / 31 neither / 2 either), only 2 rejects were not mirrored by a boundary-sibling reject — u-15228 ·No·It·Day ␣ and u-15241 ·No·It·Utter ␣ (deferred-ss04) — and both contradict their approved bare siblings u-15220/u-15221, the same double-ask pathology as the ZWNJ pair; no space reject was about the space context itself, and the rule retires those two rejects. Position-only rows are exempt and still route through kern attribution (the old font kerns across spaces and straight through ZWNJ).

Formation is unconditional and staged before the markers and the chokepoint (the prototype's proven stage order), so ·Tea·Oy forms even immediately after ZWNJ and under every stylistic set; today's pipeline renames the lead first and the ligature never forms there. Prototype divergence 5 / M1-PLAN expected class 6. Round-1 verdict: 32 approvals ratify the intent (the four "·May should use the loop stance" skip-notes are superseded by the user's final taste — ·May settles on the loop stance with its full exit terminal, no pull-back). The boundary-echo blanket (above) now takes the post-ZWNJ flavor; this entry keeps the ss03 and post-namer-dot rows.

Today's calt_post_liga_left_cleanup_pred reverts the pre-predecessor's join whenever the predecessor withdraws before the entryless ligature, over-reaching onto seams the withdrawal never touched (the never-ported demote/cleanup mechanism, recon section 13.4). Settlement withdraws exactly the one declined exit; the unrelated join one position left survives. The ·X·Day·Tea·No family (11 windows verdicted neither, echo e-0060) left this class the other way: ·Day now also yields before ·Tea·No at a run end (the then-boundary record), full ·Tea joins ·No.alt at the baseline through qsTea's order with no new ·Tea/·No record, and the 84 rows (with ·Day·Tea·No·dot, u-9176, previously either) moved to UNMATCHED pending fresh verdicts of the third form.

Under ss03 the window join-count maximization buys chains today's one-pair-at-a-time cascade cannot see. Two shapes, one mechanism: ·Tea·May·Tea and ·May·May·Tea gain the second join on the ·May·Tea side (prototype deviation 3 / M1-PLAN expected class 7), and ·It·May·Tea gains the first join — today ·May wears the entryless after-xheight-exit stance toward the half-·Tea, so the unentered ·It cannot reach it; settlement's ·May cell carries both anchors (en-y0 and the extended ex-y5), so the ·It·May baseline join lands alongside the kept ·May·Tea join. 36 of the 120 original rows are the ·It·May·Tea shape (12 per ss03-bearing configuration). Round-1 verdict: 40 approvals; u-0356's post-ZWNJ ·Tea·It join keeps its gain but its connector returned to the unextended width when qsIt's halves entry-extension record was deleted.

A third shape joined 2026-07-04 (the blessing-pass verdicts u-6645/6646/6647 and the ss03 full-·Tea rejects u-6550/6551/6553/6642/6643): full ·Tea's x-height entry unlock (qsTea full's ss03 unlock, gated on a follower in `can-enter-at-baseline`) lets an x-height exiter reach the full bar, and where the follower actually accepts the bar's baseline exit the whole window chains — ·Utter·Tea·Day and kin now render `·X ~x~ ·Tea(full) ~b~ ·Y` where the old font drew the half stub and dropped the forward join. The gate is deliberately capability-grained with no except list (the user's call, 2026-07-04, made off a rendered side-by-side of both worlds): before a follower that cannot accept the join (·Pea, ·It, a second ·Tea) the entered full bar stands with its lower half dangling instead of the half stub, and ·X·Tea·No chains into the alternate ·No exactly as the default config does — superseding the u-1329-flavor approvals of the half-stub-and-break shapes. This is the ratified ss03 meaning (full-size bar when a baseline-joiner follows, else the half stub) and grew the class from 120 to 696 rows; the new rows still await family-level blessing on the review surface like every other member.

Today's cascade drops the ·Pea·Pea y6 join whenever the second ·Pea also joins rightward (the recon section 6.3 cascade-residue family, in-alphabet flavor); settlement keeps both joins because capability and refusals permit them and join count is maximized. A strict join gain on baseline-verified capability. Round-1 verdict: 15 approvals.

Round-1 verdict: rejected — the bulk of the class (qsIt's transcribed halves-minus-qsPea x-height entry-extension record, 1,055 of the original 1,218 rows) was reverted by deleting that record; the shipped font never realized it ("this widens the ·Tea·It extension for no reason"). The surviving rows are two documented residues. (1) The exemplar's phenomenon: under ss03, when ·May joins from ·Pea/·Tea at the baseline and also extends its x-height exit toward a following half-·Tea, settlement composes en-ext-1 + ex-ext-1 on one cell where today's cascade drops the entry extension; the verdict signal there is contradictory (10 rejects on ·Pea·May·Tea-shaped words against u-0468's approval and the 40 ss03-chain approvals of the identical cell), no clean revert exists in the closed when: vocabulary (entry-side extend and contract do not net at name grain), and one question is open with the user — keep the composed extension everywhere, or feature-scoped engine work to drop it. (2) Regrouping residuals: in [X]·Oy·It·May shapes the round-1 restored ·It·May baseline join carries ·May's en-ext-1 because "the predecessor's predecessor is entered" is not expressible in the closed when: vocabulary; the residual is the same single-extension connector approved 28 times in same-seam-extension-non-summing.
Round-2 verdict: the round-1 open question resolves toward reject. The user re-triaged both residues and rejected them firmly — 15 ·Pea·May·Tea-under-ss03 windows ("pea-may": the composed en-ext-1 + ex-ext-1) and 12 [X]·Oy·It·May windows ("it-may": the restored ·It·May baseline join's en-ext-1) — 27 reject units in this class. The round-1 contradiction is now understood, not contradictory: the approved siblings (u-0393 ·Pea·May·Tea·Tea, u-0468) are the cases where ·May pulls back and never composes ex-ext-1, so they carry no summed extension; the user rejects the summing and keeps the single extension. An exhaustive, build-tested lever hunt (25 candidate records across 5 independent lever families — qsMay right/self-scoped suppression, extend-narrowing + non-summing, qsPea/qsTea predecessor-exit, qsIt two-side, ligature/same-seam — each scratch-built against a harness proven byte-identical to the oracle) found zero closed-vocabulary record that reverts any reject to old ink without collateral. The wall is a depth-2 left-context predicate the frozen when: grammar cannot express: for "pea-may", ·May's immediate-left predecessor is byte-identical (qsPea, full, baseline exit, vertical, joined_at baseline) in the bare reject and the APPROVED ·Pea·Pea·May·Tea, differing only in the predecessor's own entry (none vs y6); for "it-may" it is the predecessor's predecessor (·Oy), and the reject ·Oy·It·May is ink-identical to the approved ·Oy·It·May·Tea but for the 4th glyph. The token grammar compounds it: an extend always emits en-ext-1 (a competing more-specific extend re-emits it — build-confirmed 0 collateral but 0 revert), a contract coexists without netting (round-1's result, reproduced as 51 unmatched), and a refuse collapses the whole ·Pea→·May / ·It→·May cell rather than dropping the token. Disposition: no records authored; the class stays reviewed-rejected with these 27 windows as the documented engine-limited residue. Honoring the verdicts is one coherent feature-scoped engine task — extend same-seam non-summing to also fire on the follower's own summed exit (the ss03 "pea-may" case) plus a depth-2 left-context predicate (the "it-may" case) — surfaced for a future milestone.
Resolution (baseline-entry removal): the round-2 engine-limited residue — the 15 "pea-may" and 12 "it-may" windows — is gone, without the engine milestone. Removing qsMay's baseline-entry extend record makes ·May's baseline entry never extend, so those windows reconverge to the old ink at the entry seam and leave this class; the pixel the old font drew in ordinary words is now recorded as the intended may-baseline-entry-extension-dropped. What remains in this class is the surviving x-height entry-extension (the halves-that-exit-at-x-height record on the follower) — the new exemplar ·Day·Utter·May, where ·May's x-height entry extends after the ligature's x-height exit.
Resolution (record deletion): all ten transcribed records of the shape are gone. The oracle-proven parity-reverts (qsDay, qsOy, both qsPea stances, qsMay's grounded-loop, qsDay_qsUtter's own, and the never-firing qsTea/qsUtter twins) were deleted outright; ·No's record — half-real, since the old font draws its extension after half-·Pea and half-·Tea — fell to the no-xheight-entry-extension-dropped adjudication, and ·May's loop record to may-ligature-seam-loosened. The 3 surviving rows are the ss03 composition where the ligature's kept baseline en-ext-1 sums with its own exit extension on one cell while the old font drops the entry side — the ligature cousin of the same-seam non-summing engine wall.

Extensions never sum on one seam (design section 6.2): when the predecessor's exit already carries the seam's extra pixel, the follower's entry extension is suppressed. Today's pipeline applies both on these windows. Prototype divergence 3 / M1-PLAN expected class 4. Round-1 verdict: 28 approvals / 2 rejects / 3 eithers; the 2 rejects (u-0636 "new way has a worse ·May·It join", u-0656 "the old way seems nicer to write out by hand") contradict the 28 same-phenomenon approvals at window grain and honoring them would repeal the non-summing law, so they are presumed noise pending one ruling — re-present them next to u-0637/u-0654/u-0663.
Round-2 verdict: the two re-presented rejects (u-0417 ·Pea·May·It·May, u-0437 ◊ZWNJ ·May·It·May) were re-confirmed as rejects by the user. The build-tested lever hunt confirms there is no closed-vocabulary record that flips them to old ink without collateral: the only mechanism that drops ·May's en-ext-1 is this same non-summing suppression, which fires solely on the immediate-left predecessor's exit extension, so honoring the rejects would either repeal the 28-window non-summing law or require the same depth-2 left-context predicate the engine does not have. Status stays reviewed-approved (the 28 approvals govern the class); these 2 windows stay documented engine-limited residue. (The sibling halves-entry-extension-restored 27 they were bracketed with are since resolved by removing qsMay's baseline-entry extend record — see may-baseline-entry-extension-dropped — but that lever does not reach these two: they are same-seam windows where the predecessor's own ex-ext-1 drives the suppression, so ·May's baseline entry is beside the point and the depth-2 left-context predicate is still what an engine fix would need.)

The old font stretched half-·Day's (and half ·Day·Utter's) baseline entry by one pixel after the ·Tea·Oy ligature; the runes' baseline extend records are scoped to bare qsTea/qsYe, the ligature is neither, so the rebuild draws the same baseline join one pixel tighter. Adjudicated 2026-07-15 with qsDay's own family from side-by-side renders of both forks: the widen alternative (qsTea_qsOy added to both extend scopes) was scratch-built and proven to restore old ink on exactly these windows with zero collateral, and declined — the drop is intended. The 19 human verdicts covering the phenomenon — all approvals from 2026-06-29, carried through every surface since, spanning the plain-·Day and ·Day·Utter flavors and the word-final rider — had already judged the tighter join right; this entry gives them their ledger home. Word-final members (exit also dropped) previously rode dangling-anchor-dropped, whose ink-identical claim they violated by this one pixel.

Today's compiled names keep anchors that never realize — a dangling exit before a non-acceptor (It·It's benign ex-y5) or an entry name at word start. Settlement's cells carry only committed anchors (E-STRANDED/lookahead closure; M1-PLAN expected class 3). The withdrawals involved are `safe`, so the ink is identical; name grain only.

When the base drawing already carries the live anchor, today's pipeline leaves the bare cmap glyph in place and joins on it; the new table always rewrites to the settled cell glyph (cell labels are never the bare name). Drawing and seam identical; name grain only. Also covers the ss10 overlay, where the new font renders the raw cmap glyph at every position while the alias for the old bare name is the anchor-free boundary cell.

The ss10 isolated overlay (conform._compare_row, the isolated_overlay_active branch) renders every letter as its anchor-free default-stance cell, so under ss10 the new font breaks every seam by design ("every seam visually a break"). The old shipped font's ss10 feature was authored before this batch's qsDay/qsNo/qsUtter — and predates qsLow, qsAh and qsI the same way, whose entry/exit anchors ride their base cmap glyphs — and never extended to isolate them, so under ss10 the old font still draws their cursive joins on the bare cmap glyphs (verified in the baseline subset: qsMay|qsDay, qsNo|qsNo, qsPea|qsLow, qsPea|qsAh, and qsPea|qsI all carry a y5-or-y0 seam under ss10, while every existing|existing pair breaks). Every row here is therefore old-font-joins / new-font-breaks on a seam touching one of the new runes — the new overlay completing an isolation the old font left incomplete. The predicate requires every lost seam to neighbor a new rune, so a hypothetical existing|existing ss10 regression would stay unmatched and fail rather than be absorbed. Windows whose ligature pair actually forms now diverge at ligation grain instead (under ss10 the new font never forms the ligature at all) and ride the sibling ss10-ligature-suppressed class below. Verification is mechanized as the Junior-equivalence oracle (rebuild.review.ink.JuniorOracle): a unit divergent only under ss10 is machine-approved when the rebuild's ss10 rendering is placed-ink-identical to the shipped Junior font — the canonical isolated rendering — once Junior's uniform one-pixel-per-letter tracking is removed, so "fully isolated" is proven per unit against Junior's actual pixels rather than blanket-exempted.

The 2026-07-04 ratification from the blessing pass's ~160 verdict notes ("Under ss10 these must be fully isolated; old font joins them, new font ligates them — both wrong", "ss10 join suppression also means don't ligate"): under the isolated overlay a ligature-forming pair renders as its components' anchor-free letter twins, so every letter stands alone. Formation stays unconditional for every other configuration, but under ss10 it never fires at all: the pre-empt lookup (emit_gsub's m1_ss10_isolated_input, defined before m1_formation so its LookupList index is lower) substitutes every letter's raw cmap glyph by its `.ss10` twin first, and the twins appear in no formation sequence, marker line, chokepoint class, or settlement input — no ligature ever exists in an ss10 buffer and each letter keeps its own cluster. The old font forms qsDay_qsUtter and qsTea_qsOy under ss10 and keeps drawing their seams, so every ss10 window containing a formable E653:E67A or E652:E679 adjacency diverges at ligation grain — the old row carries the ligature glyph, the new rendering has one more glyph per formed pair. The classifier routes these ahead of marker-staging-ligature-formation (whose 00B7 arm would otherwise absorb the namer-dot ss10 windows) and only for config ss10 with a formable pair in the window; an ss10 ligation divergence without such a pair stays unmatched and fails rather than be absorbed. Boundary windows (space/ZWNJ) stay on the boundary-echo blanket, which outranks every cell/seam/ligation-grain class. Like the sibling ss10-isolation-completed class, these units machine-approve through the Junior-equivalence oracle (rebuild.review.ink.JuniorOracle) when the rebuild's ss10 rendering matches the shipped Junior font's isolated pixels with Junior's tracking removed; on the 2026-07-04 surface the oracle agreed with all 2,391 recorded human approvals of ss10-only units and refused only the five lowered-namer-dot boundary windows.

Position-only residue the comparison marks kern-attributable: the oracle gate shapes every seam- and ligation-identical row against the new font and diffs per-slot positions against the baseline with sidecar kerns normalized out (KernEvaluator over glyph_data/senior_quikscript_kerning.yaml; the in-alphabet kerned pairs are ·Oy·Pea at -3, ·Oy·Oy at -1, and — since qsLow — ·Low·May, ·Low·Low, and ·Low·Utter, each at -1), so residue can only be a kern the normalization mis-modeled or a ZWNJ-adjacency artifact — the predicate requires the drifted slots to sit on such a pair, and any other position drift matches nothing and fails. Expected zero; kept as the explicit triage channel per M1-PLAN section 6 class 9; retire at review if still zero at cutover.

The new engine adds a ·No-chain join the old font left broken — ·No reaching forward to ·Oy at the x-height, ·It rising into ·No, and the other join-maximizer gains around ·No. A taste call: keep the richer joins or restore the old breaks.
·Tea·It now joins at the x-height (before ·Day/·Utter) where the old font broke. Resembles the entered-·It x-height gains already accepted; adjudicate whether this window should join too.
·Oy·It now joins at the baseline before ·No (a strict +1-pixel join) where the old font broke.
·May/·Utter reach-back gains — ·May·Utter joining at the x-height and the ·Utter·May reach-backs (including the post-ZWNJ ·Utter·May·X windows) the old font did not draw.

The new engine breaks (or lowers) a seam the old font joined — ·No's flipped exit withdrawing before ·Tea, the ·Utter/·No chain-flip lowering x-height joins to the baseline, ·It withdrawing before ·Utter. The context-dependent, partly engine-limited family flagged in the round-2 analysis.
The seams are unchanged but the lead settles as a different cell because a composed extension no longer sums — the ·Tea·Oy·Day extension-drop window and its kin.
Default-config UNMATCHED windows that fit none of the named seam-gain or seam-loss signatures — the catch-all so no window is ever dropped from review.
